title: The factory floor
learning_goal: Open the data factory one station at a time: one solver step, one labelled file, the life of one campaign, and a new instrument for the critic; see which parts are measured, which are estimated, and which wait for a run.
takeaway: Reproducibility is designed in: every number on screen traces back to a file, a commit and a catalog row.
notes: Status (D4): X5.1, X5.2 and X5a.Q ready; X5.3 and X5.4 were PROVISIONAL in the outline and are now pending (no CPU run: the palier1 sweep and the X-point extractor are not run for the film). Each pending scene ships as an empty seat with a READY anchor (X5.3: the pipeline walk-through, SCHEMATIC, plus the measured test campaigns of infra/README.md:375 and :389; X5.4: an analytic toy potential whose X- and O-points are exact), the bet, CONFIDENCE, the criterion with its source and an ASK box, and a result variant written for both outcomes. Seat types: X5.3 gauge (tasks finished, 0 to 11), X5.4 curve (histograms of X-point counts); ch10 already uses curve, map and lamps. Seat ASK boxes: X5.3 'Where do campaigns run first: lab GPUs, Jean Zay, or a rented VM?' (logistics, R:1218, RECOMMANDATION-CLOUD §0); X5.4 'Which topology metric, and what gap in counts fails a model?', expanded into the question card X5a.Q (category framing, ask C. Nore / Y. Ponty, n null until the question register numbers it; distinct from ch06.Q, which asks which statistics in general). DATA. No data file for X5.1 and X5.2: the CPU step time (C:153) and the memory figures (C:176) are quoted from the computing page and carried in entry.params with their sources, as 10.2 carries '68 automated tests' in a chip; if CONTRACT §5 is read strictly, tools/data_existing.py could add a small 'site_facts' file (step time, peak factor, 717 MB, 0.4 / 6 / 48 GB). X5.3 reads data/x5_campaign_trace.json (converter trace) and data/palier1_sweep.json (converter palier1, the same file as 10.3); X5.4 reads data/x5_xpoints.json (converter xpoints). REQUESTS (foundation engineer B, tools/data_cloud.py). (1) As ch10 asked: add the booleans met / not_met / inconclusive to every converter's 'fields' (exactly one true); the 'meaning' sentences of X5.3 and X5.4 use them and drop silently without them. (2) conv_trace: a 'value' (= totals.done) for the gauge seat, and a 'verdict' entry in 'fields' (today only the root has it, with an underscore). (3) xpoint_count over-counts saddles on a generic smooth field: on the toy of X5.4 (7 saddles, found by Newton's method on the closed form) it returns 11, 8, 10, 10 at 32², 64², 128², 256²; on a second toy with 9 saddles, 9, 11, 13, 11. The test 'both components of grad a change sign on the cell corners' accepts cells where the two zero lines pass without crossing; the selftest (cos x cos y) cannot see it. Suggest a bilinear-zero test per cell (the 2D Haynes–Parnell method of P8:1497) or Newton refinement with de-duplication, an O-point count with the free check #X = #O per snapshot, and a selftest on a non-separable field. CHANGES AGAINST THE OUTLINE. X5.1: memory drawn as measured (solid, 128³ peak 717 MB) versus estimated (dashed, 6 and 48 GB) with the 15x factor apart from the state (B14), the GPU-card lines of C:176, and the chip 'no GPU timing yet'. X5.2: the checksum is placed in the catalog (file table), not in the file, as the site says; 'checksummed, not tamper-proof' (C10); the ingest route and what it does not restore (C:98). X5.3: the trace becomes the bet 'all eleven tasks finish' (the converter's rule, a factory check, not a PhD-plan criterion); the full per-η sweep (F7) is drawn only in the result variant, from palier1_sweep.json. X5.4: the E2 samples are no longer used (counting X-points on them would be a new run, D4); the anchor is an analytic toy on the periodic square; a predict beat is added (hold 2.5 s: more X-points or more O-points?), answered by the Poincaré–Hopf balance; the criterion states that the plan lists the metric without a pass mark (T:902-903), hence the question card. Register: X5.1 opens the module with a T3 ink change NIGHT to BLUEPRINT in its 1.6-s lead-in (10.3 is NIGHT), with the module tag and the rail L4 to L4; X5.4 changes back to NIGHT in its 1.0-s lead-in; X1 after the module is NIGHT. CUES. In X5.3 and X5.4 the seat paragraph opens on the cue 'seat' in both variants, and every formula sits on a cue that both variants share (rows; lines, answer, seat); Kit.seat resolves every cue it is given, so each seat carries two cue maps, params.seat.cues (pending) and params.seat.cues_result (result). SYMBOLS. η is said 'diffusivities' (green), as ch10; P injection and ε dissipation in the result strips, as 10.3; no s, no λ. LEXICON (audio engineer): 'X-point' and 'O-point' should be read 'ex point' and 'oh point' (pin if the voice hesitates); 'The Well' as words; no other new term in the narration (Fourier, FFT, Lawson, Leray, Poincaré–Hopf, HDF5 and UUID stay on screen only). PACE. Words budgeted with the assembler's formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail): see the table in the writer's report; every scene within ±10 % of its target.

scenes.title: One solver step

badge.note: CPU timing and memory · estimates dashed · C:153, C:176

params.note: no data file: the two CPU measurements and the memory estimates are quoted from the computing page (C:153, C:176) and carried here with their sources; the bars are drawn from these values, never typed in the page

ink_change.how: T3: a thin --infra line drawn left to right; the blueprint grid wipes in behind its tip

grid.note: 11 points per direction drawn, as the site figure; the real cutoff is |m| ≤ 21 at 64³ (C:155)

sentences.text: Open one oven: the solver keeps {u}flow{/} and {b}field{/} as waves, where a curl is a multiplication.
Products are easier on the grid, so each step hops over and back.
It trims the outer third of the waves, so products cannot fold back as fakes.
A projection keeps both fields divergence-free; the smudging is solved exactly.
One step at sixty-four cubed: eight hundredths of a second, on a processor.
The memory peak, about fifteen times the state, is an estimated six gigabytes at two hundred fifty-six cubed.

labels: u × ω + j × B · u × B
Lawson RK4 · diffusion solved exactly · 4 evaluations per step
milady.sim.mhd3d · periodic 3D MHD · PyTorch, CPU or GPU
64³ dynamic step: 0.08 s · development CPU, 2 threads

formulas.tex: \text{kept: } |m_i| \le \lfloor (N-1)/3 \rfloor \ \ (= 21 \text{ at } N = 64):\ \text{quadratic products cannot alias onto kept modes (2/3 rule)}

\hat{\mathbf P}(\mathbf k) = \mathbf I - \mathbf k\mathbf k^{\mathsf T}/|\mathbf k|^{2};\qquad \text{Lawson RK4: RK4 on } e^{\cp{\nu} k^{2} t}\,\hat{\U}\ \text{and}\ e^{\etaP k^{2} t}\,\hat{\B}\text{: diffusion integrated exactly, 4 right-hand sides per step}

\text{state } (\U, \B) = 6\,N^{3} \times 4 \text{ bytes (float32)} \approx 0.4 \text{ GB at } N = 256;\ \ \text{peak} \approx 15 \times \text{state (measured once, CPU, } 128^{3}\text{: 717 MB)} \Rightarrow \approx 6 \text{ GB at } 256^{3},\ \approx 48 \text{ GB at } 512^{3}

chips: no GPU timing yet · python -m milady.sim.mhd3d bench --device cuda measures it on site
peak ≈ 15 × state: measured once at 128³ on CPU, extrapolated · check with nvidia-smi

sentences.text: Open one jar: each run seals one file, laid out like The Well, a reference collection of simulations for machine learning.
Inside: the {u}velocity{/} and the {b}magnetic field{/}, snapshot after snapshot, and time series of energies and divergences.
The file carries a unique identifier and the code's commit.
The catalog row repeats that identifier and adds a checksum; the simulation rows can be rebuilt from files alone.
Checksummed, not sealed: a forced rewrite updates the checksum.

sentences.text: Follow one campaign down the line. One command reads the recipe: the flat sheet, eleven {param}diffusivities{/}.
The launcher opens one task per setting; each integrates sixteen runs side by side and seals one file.
For each task, the ledger gains a row with its status, its file's checksum and its wall time.
None of this has run yet. The bet: all eleven tasks finish, each with a checksummed file.
Small test campaigns already did, in seconds, and a comparable workload once took about half an hour.

sentences.text: A new instrument for the critic: in the flat sheet, {b}field lines{/} are contours of one potential.
Each island has an O-point at its centre; where lines cross, an X-point.
In this periodic box, which kind is more common?
Neither: exactly as many of each, a free check on any counter.
The internship offer asks for topology; the report's experiments computed none.
The plan lists X-point counts among its metrics, but sets no pass mark.

scenes.visual: Render class flat (one Canvas for the contour lines, SVG for marks, cards and the seat). Register NIGHT: T3 ink change from BLUEPRINT in the 1.0-s lead-in (params.ink_change; whoosh at 0.1 s, -22 dB). LEFT, the toy (params.toy, a 600 x 600 square at x 140-740, y 160-760): the potential a(x, y) = Σ A cos(kx x + ky y + φ) with params.toy.modes is evaluated in setup on a params.toy.grid² grid and contoured (marching squares, params.toy.levels levels, precomputed polylines): positive levels in --b, negative levels in --b-neg (two senses of circulation, shades of one hue, never a new colour). The square's edges are dashed grey with small paired arrow ticks marking that opposite edges are glued (periodic box). Kit.chip kind 'schematic' 'SCHEMATIC · toy field on the periodic square' under the tile. P1. On 'lines-0.15': the contours draw on (1.2 s, innermost first); label 'field lines = contours of the potential a'. On 'points-0.15': the O-point params.toy.points[highlight.O] gets a filled vermillion dot that pulses once, leader label 'O-point · island centre'; at 55 % of the sentence the X-point points[highlight.X] gets a cross, the contour through it (the separatrix, level = its a value) brightens to 100 % while the others drop to 50 %, leader label 'X-point · lines cross'. On 'predict-0.15': a predict card at params.predict_card (the film's predict style, as 08.2: kicker 'PREDICT', line 'periodic box: more X-points or more O-points?'); the hold comes from the script (hold_after 2.5 s); during the hold the contours breathe (opacity ±8 %, 2-s period). On 'answer-0.15': the predict card leaves; every critical point of params.toy.points appears in a seeded order (60 ms apart), dots for O, crosses for X; two tally columns rise beside the tile (params.tally: one of dots, one of crosses, one mark per point) and stop at the same height (no digits); Kit.pen kind 'check' beside them with the label 'saddles = extrema on the torus · Poincaré–Hopf'; pop at 'answer+0.2'. P3. On 'seat-0.15': the toy and the tally shrink to the left third (x 140-620, 0.8 s); Kit.seat(ctx, {...params.seat, cues: ctx.variant === 'result' ? params.seat.cues_result : params.seat.cues, variant: ctx.variant, data: ctx.data.seat}) of type 'curve' opens on the right (frame x 860-1420, y 200-640): dashed grey frame, x axis 'X-points per snapshot' with no ticks yet (only the end words 'fewer' and 'more'), y axis 'share of snapshots' from 0 to 1, a dashed amber bracket over an empty band labelled 'tolerance: not set' (the success band exists, its width is the question), grey tag 'DATA · X5_XPOINTS · AWAITING'; right column: THE BET and CONFIDENCE low with the line params.seat.why. Kit.chip kind 'plain' 'a metric requested by the internship offer · none computed in the report (R:739)' under the frame. Pending only (the result has no 'criterion' cue), on 'criterion-0.15': SUCCESS CRITERION with its source; at 'criterion+1.6' the boxed ASK BEFORE WE COMPUTE (params.seat.ask). RESULT (when data/x5_xpoints.json exists; the result narration keeps the cues lines, points, predict, answer and seat, then verdict and meaning): on 'seat-0.15' the seat opens with params.seat.cues_result, its frame solid, the x axis takes the integer ticks of data.seat.bins, and two step histograms draw on: data.seat.counts_reference as a white solid outline (simulated, white chip 'simulated') and data.seat.counts_generated as a violet dashed outline (violet chip 'generated'), each normalized to a share; the seat's RESULT block shows the converter's verdict and verdict_text (no verdict computed in the page); Kit.lowerThird kind 'source' with data.seat (meta.stamp 'SIMULATED vs GENERATED · X-points', SHA-256 prefix). If the file gives a tolerance (verdict_rule), the amber band is drawn at that width around the reference mean; otherwise it keeps the label 'tolerance: not set'. DATA. x5_xpoints.json (converter tools/data_cloud.py xpoints, from reference MFF fields of palier1_mhd2d or tier 1 and an npz of generated B fields): counts_reference[], counts_generated[], bins[], verdict, verdict_rule, verdict_text, fields {mean_reference, mean_generated, verdict} plus the booleans met / not_met / inconclusive (exactly one true). Requested: O-point counts too, so the free check of this scene can run on real snapshots (see notes). Badge CONJECTURE, confidence low, note 'tier-1 metric · no pass mark yet'. Key colours: vermillion (field lines), amber (the distribution of counts and its tolerance), violet only in the result (generated). No corner needle.
